newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans higher on China talk, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans higher on China talk, weather.

text.p: Talk that China bought U.S. soybeans and was looking for additional supplies pushed CBOT soybeans higher at midsession, with forecasts for rain and snow adding momentum, traders said.
"With China around and the weather, we're going to bounce," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "We're hearing (China) bought 50,000 (tonnes) soybeans and are looking for another 50,000."
Forecasts called for rains across the eastern Corn Belt with drier conditions to the west. Another round of showers was expected to move in by the weekend.
Cash basis levels remained firm at country locations and U.S. Gulf CIF values were higher on Wednesday, which further fueled the rally, traders said.

Several brokers noted the pick-up in the cash prices, coupled with Tuesday's strong CBOT gains, sparked ideas of strong export demand. Flat soybean prices in several country locations jumped 12 cents per bushel Tuesday afternoon.
On the technical side, traders said November soybeans needed to close above $6.95 per bushel to confirm a rally.
"If we can hold above $6.95 on the close we're going to test $7.00 this week," a trader said.
Resistance was pegged near $7.00 per bushel.
At 1117 CDT, soybeans were six to 11 cents per bushel higher with November up 7-1/2 at $6.96-1/2 a bushel.
